Pd-Catalyzed Regio- and Enantioselective Aminoarylation of
Allenols with Aryl Iodides and 2 ‑Pyridones
Hongfang Li, Ijaz Khan, Meiqi Li, Zheng Wang, Xue Wu, * Kuiling Ding, * and Yong Jian Zhang *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 3567 −3572 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: A new asymmetric catalytic protocol for the
synthesis of enantioenriched N-allyl 2-pyrodones has been
developed via the ﬁrst Pd-catalyzed regio- and enantioselective
aminoarylation of allenols with aryl iodides and 2-pyridones. By
using a palladium complex generated in situ from Pd
2(dba)3·
CHCl3 and ( S,S,S)-SKP as a catalyst, the three-component
aminoarylation proceeded smoothly to a ﬀord a variety of
functionalized N-allylic 2-pyridones in high yields with good regioselectivities and excellent enantioselectivities.
C
hiral N-substituted 2-pyridones have emerged as useful
motifs in many natural products and medicinally relevant
agents, as exempli ﬁed by aspernigrin B 1 isolated from Axinella
damicornis and Aspergillus welwitschiae CUGBMF180262,
respectively, human rhinovirus 3C protease inhibitors, 2
GDC-0994 as an extracellular-signal-regulated kinase inhibitor 3
(Figure 1), and many others. 4 In this context, the development
of synthetic approaches to chiral N-substituted 2-pyridone
derivatives became an important goal in pharmaceutical
research and drug discovery. In general, they are prepared
via stereoselective nucleophilic substitution of 2-pyridones to
chiral electrophiles, or by the reaction of 2 H-pyran-2-ones with
chiral amines.
2−5 However, asymmetric catalytic protocols for
the synthesis of chiral N-substituted 2-pyridones from achiral
starting materials are less explored. In 2010, Batey and co-
workers reported ﬁrst asymmetric catalytic method to access
enantioenriched N-substituted 2-pyridones via Pd(II)-cata-
lyzed asymmetric [3,3] sigmatropic rearrangement of 2-allyloxy
pyridines ( Scheme 1 a).
6 So far, only sporadic reports on
asymmetric catalytic approaches have been documented, which
are restricted to the allylic substitution of allylic donors with 2-
pyridones catalyzed by a chiral Rh-,
7 Ir-,8 or Pd-complex 9
(Scheme 1 b ) .T h e r e f o r e ,t h ed e v e l o p m e n to feﬃcient
asymmetric catalytic methods to provide more functionalized
chiral N-substituted 2-pyrid ones from read ily accessible
starting materials is highly appealing.
Since the seminal work by Tsuji and Shimizu in 1984 on the
Pd-catalyzed aminoarylation of allenes, 10 Pd-catalyzed carbo-
functionalization of allenes with aryl halides and nucleophiles
has become a useful tool for the preparation of valuable
compounds with diverse functionalities.

Pd-catalyzed allylic alkylation of allylic substrates, 12 the three-
component reaction can avoid preinstallation of a leaving
group for the allylic donors, and allows to construct two
chemical bonds in one-pot manipulation.
13 However, the Pd-
catalyzed carbofunctionalization of allenes generally gives
linear allylic products, whereas controlling the regioselectivity
to aﬀord branched products remains elusive.
14 Furthermore, it
is important to point out that the asymmetric versions of this
type of carbofunctionalization of allenes have not yet been
documented so far to the best of our knowledge.
As an ongoing e ﬀort on the development of Pd-catalyzed
regio- and enantioselective allylic substitution
15 and cyclo-
addition,16 we are interested to develop a new asymmetric
catalytic protocol for the construction of enantioenriched N-
substituted 2-pyridones via Pd-catalyzed three-component
aminoarylation of allenols with aryl iodides and 2-pyridones.
We envisioned that the Heck-type arylation of allenol with aryl
iodides could give 2-aryl substituted allylpalladium intermedi-
ate I, which might undergo allylic substitution with 2-pyridone
to produce desired N-substituted pyridones ( Scheme 1 c).
Herein, we report the ﬁrst Pd-catalyzed regio- and
enantioselective three-component process of carbofunctional-
ization of allenes, which allows one to rapidly access more
functionalized N-substituted 2-pyridones in high yields with
good regioselectivities and excellent enantioselectivities via the
formation two chemical bonds from readily accessible starting
materials.
Initial investigation was focused on the optimization of the
conditions for the Pd-catalyzed aminoarylation using 2,3-
allenol ( 1a), iodobenzene ( 2a), and 2-pyrodone ( 3a)a s
standard substrates ( Table 1 ). The reactions were typically
performed in the presence of K
2CO3 as the base additive in
toluene at 60 °C for 16 h, with the palladium complex
generated in situ from Pd 2(dba)3·CHCl3 and a chiral ligand as
the catalyst. At the outset, some chiral ligands with di ﬀerent
skeletons and/or ligating moieties were examined (entries 1 −
8). To our delight, ( S,S,S)-SKP ( L6)17 proved to be the
optimal chiral ligand, to a ﬀord the targeting branched-product
4aa in 73% yield with 93:7 er and a b/l ratio of 80:20 (entry
6). With ( S,S,S)-SKP (L6) as a ligand, reducing the loading of
K2CO3 to 1 equiv led to an increment of er to 98:2 (entry 9).
A brief survey of the solvent e ﬀect uncovered toluene as the
optimal solvent (entries 9−13). The reactions proceeded much
better using K 2CO3 or K 3PO4 (entries 9 or 15) as the base to
aﬀord 4aa with higher enantioselectivities, demonstrating
signiﬁcant impact of base on the reaction e ﬃciency (entries
14−18 and 9).
With optimized conditions in hand ( Table 1 , entry 9), the
reaction generality was then investigated by the three
component aminoarylation of 2,3-allenol ( 1a) with 2-pyridone
(3a) and various aryl iodides 2. As shown in Figure 2 , a wide
range of aryl iodides bearing di ﬀerent steric and electronic
features tolerates the reaction conditions very well to a ﬀord the
corresponding carboaminated products 4aa−4ja in moderate
to high yields with good branched regioselectivities and
excellent enantioselectivities. While the reaction of 2-naphthyl
iodide proceeded smoothly to give the corresponding product
4ka in high yield with excellent enantioselectivity, a signi ﬁcant
drop of e ﬃciency was observed when 1-naphthyl iodide was
employed in the reaction.
The substrate scope for aryl iodides 2 and substituted 2-
pyridones 3 was subsequently studied in the reactions of 2,3-
allenol 1a (Figure 3 ). Under the optimized conditions A
(Table 1 , entry 9), the reaction with 5-methyl-2-pyridone
proceeded smoothly to furnish aminoarylated products 4ab in
good yields with moderate b/l ratio and high enantioselectivity
(98:2 er). However, moderate enantioselectivities were
observed for the reactions with other substituted 2-pyridones.
In this context, the reaction conditions were further optimized
toward the reaction of 1a with 2a and 5-nitro-2-pyridone ( 3f)
(see the Supporting Information for details). As a result, we
found that the enantioselectivity could be improved in most
cases when the reactions were conducted in the presence of
K
3PO4 as the base in methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE) as a
solvent at 30 °C for 24 h (condition B). This optimized
condition B was compatible with a diversity of aryl iodides 2 or
substituted 2-pyridones 3 bearing various functional groups,
such as nitro, aldehyde, cyanide, bromide, and 2-naphthyl
groups, to produce the corresponding adducts 4 in good yields
with moderate b/l ratios and high enantioselectivities.

component aminoarylation process, several monosubstituted

allenes 1b-1e were examined in the reaction with 2a and 3a
under the optimized conditions A (Table 1, entry 9). As shown
in Scheme 2 , the reaction of 3,4-allenol 1b with 2a and 3a
proceeded smoothly to a ﬀord corresponding aminoarylated
product 6a in high yield with high branched selectivity and
enantioselectivity. In sharp contrast, the reaction of 4,5-allenol
1c with a longer distance between hydroxyl and allenyl
moieties failed to produce the corresponding aminoarylated
product under otherwise identical conditions. In addition, 2,3-
allenol ether 1d with the hydroxyl group being blocked by n-
butyl and alkyl-substituted allene 1e were also found
incompatible with the protocol. These results implied that a
properly situated hydroxyl on the monosubstituted allene is
essential not only for the branched regioselectivity control, but
also for the reactivity. The appropriate directing e ﬀect on
hydroxyl group might be critical for the insertion step of
allenols to Ar −Pd−I intermediates. In addition, the allylpalla-
dium intermediates bearing a hydroxymethyl or hydroxyethyl
groups might build an e ﬀective hydrogen-bond interaction
with 2-pyridones,
18 which can improve the nucleophilicity of
2-pyridones on one hand, and possibly favors the branched
regioselectivity on the other. As a further demonstration, the
aminoarylation of 3,4-allenol 1b with diﬀerent aryl iodides and
substituted 2-pyridones still proceeded well to a ﬀord the
corresponding aminoarylated products 6 in high yields with
high levels of regio- and enantioselectivities.

gram-scale transformation and the elaboration of the product

aminoarylation of 1a with 2a and 3a in 7 mmol scale under
standard conditions still proceeded smoothly to give desired
product 4aa in 71% yield (1.2 g) with a 79:21 b/l ratio and
96:4 er ( Scheme 3 a). With the obtained 4aa, the further
transformation has been examined. The selective hydro-
genation of 4aa in the presence of Pd/C as a catalyst in
methanol a ﬀorded compound 7 as an only diastereomer in
95% yield ( Scheme 3 b). Next, the Prins-type cyclization
19 of
4aa with 3-nitrobenzaldehyde ( 8) was carried out in the
presence of BF 3 etherate in THF. Interestingly, the bicyclic
pyridium salt 9 bearing three stereocenters can be obtained in
75% yield with complete diastereoselectivity. The hydrolysis 20
of compound 9 with aqueous K 2CO3 proceeded smoothly to
aﬀord more functionalized chiral 2-pyridone compound 10 as
an only diastereomer in 85% yield without any deterioration of
enantiomeric purity ( Scheme 3c). The absolute con ﬁgurations
of 7 and 9 were unambiguously assigned by X-ray
crystallography (see the Supporting Information ).
In conclusion, we have developed a new asymmetric
catalytic protocol for the synthesis valuable N-substituted 2-
pyridone derivatives via the ﬁrst Pd-catalyzed enantioselective
three-component aminoarylation of allenols with aryl iodides
and 2-pyridones. By using palladium complex generated in situ
from Pd
2(dba)3·CHCl3 and ( S,S,S)-SKP as a catalyst, the
three-component aminoarylation proceeded smoothly through
the formation of a carbon −carbon and a carbon −nitrogen
bond in one pot, providing a variety of functionalized N-allylic
2-pyridones in high yields with good regioselectivities and
excellent enantioselectivities. The control experiments demon-
strated that the hydroxyl group on the allenols is essential for
the reactivity of the process and the control of the branched
selectivity. The synthetic utility of the present process has been
demonstrated by gram-scale transformation and the elabo-
ration of the product. Further investigation of this type of
three-component tandem reaction is currently underway in our
laboratory and will be reported in due course.
